_comment: Twenty large companies, one per industry, chosen so that no two share a
network-estate shape: a grocery chain, a parcel network, a bank branch
estate, a plant-and-lab estate and a mine site are different problems,
and an estimator that only ever sees stores is not being tested.
industry is the code the case is researched under. Every one of these
which are keyed by it - an industry the seed does not know falls back to
DEFAULT, and the estate stops differentiating. Entity resolution proposes
its own industry on the candidate; this is the fallback and the check.
in_scope_countries is deliberately a handful per company rather than the
whole group footprint. The countries are where the estate is dense AND
where reference.unit_cost_prior has approved rates, because a country
with sites and no rate card prices nothing and only lowers coverage.
declared_footprint is a public-disclosure fallback, used only if research
returns no promotable site counts. The manifest records which was used.

excluded.reason: the finding counts a satellite IT room in Dublin, named in an IT contractor's project page alongside Slough and Dundee. A room of equipment inside a building Tesco already occupies is not a site, and pricing it as a DC both invents a building and gives it a data centre's bandwidth.
the only source is a warehouse fit-out company's listicle of large buildings, which names one Dublin facility and states no count. The finding's own note says the total Irish DC count was not found.

a drop-off counter inside a third-party retailer. The premises are the host's and so is the access line; a DHL scanner on cellular is a device cost, not a site circuit. Same basis as the UPS Store network.

the 24,000 'person-operated sales points' are overwhelmingly counters inside partner retailers - the evidence's own note says the lower 13,000 figure 'may exclude partner/agency outlets', which means the 24,000 includes them. A counter in somebody else's shop runs on somebody else's line. Same basis as this case's already-excluded GB/SERVICE_POINT, and as the UPS Store, Fintro and Allianz rulings.
Fintro is a franchise network - independently operated agents, so the connectivity is not BNP's cost. The retained Belgian branches are declared separately.
the 1,474 retail branches in the registration document are the same network this spec declares as 1,600 FR BRANCH sites.

the 2,500 agencies are the Nordost sales region alone - the sources say 'in den neuen Bundeslaendern' and 'im Vertriebsgebiet Nordost' - promoted as a German national count, and the figure is a pre-closure baseline against which 430 agencies were due to shut in 2025. Whether a tied agent's connectivity is Allianz's cost is the separate question referred on the French agencies.
31 branches of Allianz Bank Financial Advisors from a single aggregator, with no evidence settling whether the 400 declared Italian branches already include them.

an agent general is self-employed, leases their own premises and buys their own access line; Allianz reaches them over it. The STORE archetype buys a broadband circuit with 5G backup and Allianz does not buy 2,516 of those. Same basis as the UPS Store network and BNP's Fintro branches, both already excluded.

the finding is 'Private 5G campus network - Schwarzheide site (OT layer)'. A 5G campus network is a private on-premises mobile network, not a campus: the word is a telecom term and the CAMPUS archetype means a research or manufacturing campus carrying thousands of people. Schwarzheide is an existing BASF German site already inside the declared estate, so this adds a network deployment as though it were a premises.
